## Moosend

<https://docs.everestforms.net/docs/moosend/>

This guide explains how to connect the Everest Forms plugin with Moosend to sync form submissions and generate email lists. This integration of Moosend with Everest Forms is perfect for building newsletters, lead-generation forms, or event registrations.

Prerequisites:

- A WordPress website with admin access

- Everest Forms Pro ( Moosend integration is only available in the Pro version)

- A Moosend account ( Sign up here if needed)

When users submit a specific form, their details (like email, name, phone number, etc.) are automatically added to your Moosend email list. Once you have the contact list, you can trigger email marketing automation.

## Step 1: Install Everest Forms Pro

- **Download the plugin:**

- Purchase the plugin via everestforms.net .

- Download the **Everest Forms Pro .zip** file from your** WPEverest account.2. Activate Everest Form Pro**

- In your WordPress Dashboard, navigate to **Plugins > Add New > Upload**.

- Select the downloaded** .zip **file, click** Install Now**, then **Activate**.

3**. Install Free Version:**

- If not installed, you’ll be notified to install Everest Forms Free. Click to install and activate.

4.** Activate the Everest Forms Pro**

Enter your license key to use premium features ( The license key is available in your WPEverest account dashboard ).

## Step 2: Activate the Moosend Addon

- Navigate to **Everest Forms > Addons.**

- Search for** Moosend** and toggle to enable the addon.

## Step 3: Connect Everest Forms with Moosend

### Generating Moosend API Key

- Login into your **Moosend Dashboard**

- Under **More > Settings >API key, **find the API key and copy it

Also, create an email list on Moosend before proceeding to the Everest Forms dashboard. This email list is where you’ll send the contact form data.

### Add the Moosend API key to Everest Forms

- Navigate to **Everest Forms > Settings > Integration**

- Click on the **settings **icon next to Moosend

3. Paste your Moosend API Key, add a nickname, and click **Connect to Moosend**

## Step 4: Create a Form and Configure Moosend

### Create a Form

Go to **Everest Forms > Add New** and build your form by adding the necessary form fields . ( You can also use the existing form )

- Open the **Integration tab **and click on** Add New Connection**

- Give a name to the connection and hit** OK**

### Configure Moosend Settings

**Select Account:** Confirm the Moosend account you’re connecting to; you can choose from the nickname that you created earlier.

**Select List:** Choose the Moosend list where form submissions will be sent.

**List Fields:** Map the list field between Moosend and your form fields.

- **List Fields **are the predefined fields from your Moosend list.

- **Available Form Fields **are the fields added to your Everest Forms form.

You can also create a custom field in Moosend first and then map the field in Everest Forms.

### Use Conditional Logic (Optional)

You can enable conditional logic to send data to Moosend only if specific conditions are met.

- Check the box to use the conditional logic

- Define the rules like: Send data only if the **Name **is **FrankSave** the form to apply the changes.

## Step 5: Test Moosend Integration

To test, add the form to a page or post using the form’s shortcode and publish it.

Open the page or post in incognito mode and submit the test entry.

### Check on Moosend

- Go to your **Moosend dashboard > Audience > Email list**. Click to open the connected list.

- Ensure the test submission appears here.

You’re all set! Start capturing leads and growing your email list seamlessly.

## Salesflare

<https://docs.everestforms.net/docs/salesflare-integrations/>

**Salesflare** Integrations with **Everest Forms** automatically adds form submissions to your contact list and generates leads without manual data entry. This allows instant follow-ups, seamless tracking, and better organization of your leads. Whether it’s a contact form or any other form, this integration helps you nurture prospects and convert them into customers more efficiently.

**Prerequisites:**

- A WordPress website with admin access

- Everest Forms Pro ( Salesflare integrations is a Pro feature)

- A Salesflare account ( Sign up here if needed)

## Step 1: Install Everest Forms Pro

- **Download the plugin:**

- Purchase **Everest Forms Pro** via everestforms.net .

- Log into your **WPEverest account**, navigate to Downloads, and download the **Everest Forms Pro .zip** file.

- **Upload & Activate Everest Form Pro**

- In your WordPress Dashboard, navigate to **Plugins > Add New > Upload**.

- Upload the **.zip **file, click** Install Now**, then **Activate**.

- **Install the Free Version:**

- If not installed, you’ll be notified to install Everest Forms Free. Click to install.

- **Activate your License**

- Enter your license key to use premium features ( The license key is available in your WPEverest account dashboard ).

Here's our detailed installation guide for the Everest Forms Pro plugin .

## Step 2: Activate the Salesflare Addon

Salesflare integrations require you to use the Salesflare addon. So,

- Go to **Everest Forms > Addons.**

- Search for **Salesflare **and toggle the switch to** enable **it.

## Step 3: Connect Everest Forms to Salesflare

### Get Your Salesflare API Key

- Log in to your Salesflare Dashboard .

- Go to **Settings > API Keys**.

- Click **Generate API Key** and copy the key.

### Add the Salesflare API Key to Everest Forms

- Go to **Everest Forms > Settings > Integrations**.

- Click the **Settings icon** next to **Salesflare**.

3. Paste the **Salesflare API key**, add a nickname, and click **Connect to Salesflare**.

## Step 4: Create a Form & Configure Salesflare Integrations

### Create a Form

Go to **Everest Forms > Add New** and build your form by adding necessary form fields (e.g., add Name , Email , Phone ). You can also use the existing form to integrate Salesflare.

### Enable Salesflare Integrations

- Open your form editor and go to the **Integrations** tab.

- Click **Add New Connection**, name it (e.g., “Salesflare Leads”), and click **OK**.

### Configure Salesflare Settings

- **Select Account**: Confirm your Salesflare account (auto-detected if only one exists).

- **Select List:** Select the contact list where you want to add contacts

- **List Fields: **From here, map the fields between Salesflare and your form.

- ** List Fields (left): ** It has the default fields like Email , First Name , Company , and Phone from Salesflare

- ** Available Form Fields (right): **You can find the fields added to your contact form using the drop-down menu.

### Conditional Logic (Optional)

Enable **Use conditional logic** to sync data only if rules are met (e.g., Sync contact only if the last name is Sainz )

Click **Save** to apply the changes.

Here's a step-by-step guide on using conditional logic on your form fields .

## Step 5: Test the Salesflare Integrations

### Embed the Form

Add the form to a page/post using the provided shortcode or block. You can also click on th**e Embed **option at the top-right corner of the form to add the form to an existing or new page.

### Submit a Test Entry

Open the page in incognito mode and submit the form with test data.

### Verify in Salesflare

- Log in to Salesflare and go to **Contacts** or **Leads**.

- Confirm the test entry appears with mapped fields and tags.

Contact synced with Salesflare after form submission through Everest Forms

This confirms that you have successfully integrated Salesflare into your form. You can use this contact list to nurture leads, automate follow-ups, and more.

## GetGist

<https://docs.everestforms.net/docs/getgist/>

**Everest Forms **GetGist add-on allows you to synchronize Everest Forms with GetGist.

## Installation

- Firstly, you need to purchase the Everest Forms pro plugin.

- After the successful purchase, you will get the plugin zip file under your WPEverest account page.

- Through your WordPress Dashboard, visit **Plugins -> Add New -> Upload** and then choose the downloaded zip file, and then install and activate it.

- Then, go to **Everest Forms Dashboard -> All Features -> GetGist**

- Click on the toggle button to activate GetGist.

- Now you are ready to use this add-on for your site.

Now, follow the instructions below to **integrate GetGist with Everest Forms**:

## Set up GetGist Account:

To use this feature, you must have a GetGist Account that you will need to connect with the Everest Forms.

If you already have an Account then please find the **GetGistAPI key** of your **GetGist account** since you will need them for connection. You can find them in your GetGist account: https://getgist.com/

## Configuring GetGist Account in Everest Forms

After you have got the keys, you will need to enter the ** API key** and **NickName** to **Everest Forms** settings.

Navigate to **Everest Forms->Settings->Integration->**GetGist and click on **Add New Connection **button.

Enter the ** API Key** and GetGist** Nick Name** and click on **Connect to **GetGist.

You can also **connect multiple **GetGist** API**.

## Integrating GetGist Lists with Forms

After you have **added the keys** to the **Everest Forms settings**, now you need to** connect it to the contact form** you made.

To do so, **Click** on **Everest Forms** > **All Forms** >**(click on the form you want to connect)**

Then, go to **Integration->GetGist** and click on **Add new connection.** Give a name to the connection.

On the right, you can **Select Account** with which you have created your list. Also, you can add a new account from there.

Now, on the **Select List** option, choose the GetGist** list** that you created.

Finally, map **Everest Forms** fields to GetGist** List Fields**.

## Select/Create Tags

You can either select the GetGist tags or add new tags. To add a new tag, just write the name of the tag and click on ‘**Add New Tags**‘.

## Conditional Logic for Adding Subscribers

**Use Conditional Logic**: You may want users to **subscribe to **GetGist** only if **they fill certain fields with certain values. For example, in the above case (see image above), the users will only be added to the GetGist list if they enter **John** in the **First Name** input.

## CleverReach

<https://docs.everestforms.net/docs/clever-reach/>

**Everest Forms Cleverreach** feature allows you to synchronize Everest Forms with CleverReach.

## Installation

- Firstly, you need to purchase the Everest Forms pro plugin.

- After the successful purchase, you will get the plugin zip file under your WPEverest account page.

- Now, you can download the Everest Forms pro plugin.

- Through your WordPress Dashboard, visit **Plugins -> Add New -> Upload** and then choose the downloaded zip file and then install and activate it.

- Then, go to **Everest Forms -> Dashboard -> All Features -> CleverReach**

- Click on the toggle button to activate **CleverReach**.

- Now you are ready to use this add-on for your site.

Now, follow the instructions below to **integrate CleverReach with Everest Forms**:

## Set up Cleverreach Account:

To use this feature, you must have an Cleverreach Account that you will need to connect with the Everest Forms.

If you already have an Account then please find the **Client ID** and the** Client Secret** of your **CleverReachaccount**, since you will need them for connection. You can find them in your CleverReach account by following this doc: https://rest.cleverreach.com/howto/

If you do not have an CleverReach Account then you will need to create an account first and then come back to this documentation to set up the connection.

## Configuring CleverReach Account in Everest Forms

After you have got the **client Id** and **client Secret**, you will need to enter the CleverReach Client ID and **CleverReach Client Secret** to **Everest Forms** settings.

Navigate to **Everest Forms->Settings->Integration->CleverReach** and click on **Add New Connection **button.

Enter the **CleverReach Client ID and **CleverReach Client Secret and CleverReach** Nick Name** and click on **Get Access code**.

After that a new tab, and click on **Log in with my existing CleverReach account and connect button**. Now, you have to enter your **Customer ID, User name and Password.**

You will get the access code now enter that copied access code in **Access Code **input field then click on **Connect to CleverReach button**.

You can also **connect multiple **CleverReach** API**.

## Integrating CleverReach Lists with Forms

**Note:** You have to create lists in your CleverReach Account. The created list will be shown in the CleverReach Individual Form Settings after you connect it to the Everest Forms.

After you have **added the keys** to the **Everest Forms settings**, now you need to** connect it to the contact form** you made.

To do so, **Click** on **Everest Forms** > **All Forms** >**(click on the form you want to connect)**

Then, go to **Integration->CleverReach** and click on **Add new connection.** Give a name to the connection.

On the right, you can **Select Account** with which you have created your list. Also, you can add a new account from there.

Now, on the **Select List** option, choose the **CleverReach list** that you created.

Finally, map **Everest Forms** fields to **CleverReach List Fields**.

## Conditional Logic for Adding Subscribers

**Use Conditional Logic**: You may want users to **subscribe to ClevereReach only if **they fill certain fields with certain values. For example, in the above case (see image above), the users will only be added to the Cleverreach list if they enter **John** in the **First Name** input.

## AWeber Integration

<https://docs.everestforms.net/docs/aweber-integration/>

AWeber and Everest Forms can be integrated to allow subscribers to be added to your list directly through an Everest Forms form. This documentation will guide you through the process of integrating these two services.

## Installation

- Go to **Everest Forms > Add-ons > Modules.**

- Search for ‘AWeber’ and activate it.

Please note that you need Everest Forms Pro installed and activated in your site to use this.

## Configuration

Once you have activated the AWeber, follow the steps below to configure it so that you can send data to the desired lists.

- Go to **Everest Forms > Settings > Integration > AWeber.**

- Click on the **Settings** button.

### Generating AWeber Client ID

You will need the AWeber Client ID to get the access code. To generate the Client ID, follow the steps below.

- Log in to your AWeber Developer Account.

- Go to **My Apps **and Create a new app.

- While creating the app, make sure the following things are correct.

- **Client Type**: Confidential

- **OAuth Redirect URL**: https://yoursuite.com/wp-admin/?evf_aweber_auth=1

- Click on **Create App. **You will then get the Client ID.

- Copy this Client ID to a clipboard.

### Integrating AWeber with Everest Forms

- Go to **Everest Forms > Settings > Integration > AWeber.**

- Enter the Client ID and click on the **Get Access Code**.

- Add the access code and Client Secret(from your app in the AWeber account).

- Click on **Connect to AWeber.**

You can disconnect the current connection or also add multiple connections.

### Sending data from Everest Forms to AWeber

Once you have successfully connected your AWeber account to the Everest Forms, follow the steps below to send data to the AWeber.

- Go to **Everest Forms > All Forms.**

- Choose the desired form and click on **Edit.**

- Go to the **Integrations > AWeber.**

- Click on Add New Connection.

- Provide the connection name and click on the **OK** button.

- Now, you can map the form fields to the AWeber list.

#### Using Conditional Logic

**Use Conditional Logic**: You may want users to **subscribe to AWeber only if **they fill certain fields with certain values. For example, in the above case (see image above), the users will only be added to the Active Campaign list if they enter **J**ack in the **First Name** input.

## Airtable

<https://docs.everestforms.net/docs/airtable/>

## Installation

- Firstly, you need to purchase the Everest Forms Pro plugin.

- After the successful purchase, you will get the plugin zip file under your WPEverest account page.

- Now, you can download the **Everest Forms Pro** from there.

- Through your WordPress Dashboard, visit **Plugins -> Add New -> Upload** and then choose the downloaded zip file, and then install and activate it.

- Now go to **Everest Forms > Add-ons > All Features.**

- Search **Airtable **add-on and install it.

## Configuration

To integrate Airtable with your contact forms, you will need an Airtable API key.

### Generating Airtable API key

- Either login to your OnePageCRM account or create a new account .

- Once you’re logged in, you can click on profile image icon on top right corner of navbar. From there, click “**Account**”.

- You can create **Access Token** from this Link

- Give a name for your token, select these scope **data.records:read**, **data.records:write** and **schema.bases:read** by clicking Add a scope .

By clicking on **Create Token,** the token will be created.

Copy this key to your clipboard and enter it on the Everest Forms > Settings > Integration > Airtable. Then, click on **Connect to Airtable.**

It will then be connected to the Everest Forms. If you want to disconnect this app, you can click on the Disconnect button on the far right.

Similarly, you can add multiple connections.

### Connect Airtable to your contact forms

Once you have connected the Airtable to the Everest Forms settings, you need to create a form to connect it to the **AirtableSchema**. You can connect your existing forms as well. To do this, go to the following location:

`All Forms > Choose a Form > Integration > OnePageCRM`

- Click on **Add New Connection.**

- Provide a nickname for the connection.

- Now, you have to choose the Account, Base, Schema, and map the form fields as required.

- Click on **Save.**

#### How to use conditional logic for Airtable connections?

To use conditional logic, enable the option by ticking the ‘**Use Conditional Logic’ **option at the bottom of every connection you make.

In the above example, the form sends data to the Airtable account only if the Name is ‘Everest’.

## MailPoet

<https://docs.everestforms.net/docs/mailpoet/>

Connect your Everest Forms data to your Mailpoet accounts. Use Mailpoet API to link Everest Forms with Mailpoet, syncing your website’s form submissions with the Mailpoet subscriber list.

## Installation

- Firstly, you need to purchase the Everest Forms Pro plugin.

- After the successful purchase, you can activate the module from** EverestForms > Addons > All Features > All Modules**.

- Search** Mailpoet **add-on and **activate **it by clicking on the toggle button.

- Install and activate the **MailPoet** plugin.

You will have to install and activate the MailPoet plugin for this to work. Click here to download and install this plugin.

## Setup and Configuration

Once you have activated the MailPoet integration, go to **Everest Forms** > **Settings** > **Integration **> **MailPoet **and click on the settings button. This will take you to the configuration screen for the MailPoet integration.

## Getting the MailPoet Activation Key

After you install and activate the MailPoet plugin.

- Go to **WPDashboard > MailPoet** and click on the **Begin Setup** button.

- After you click onthe **Begin Setup** button, you will be redirected to next page and tick mark the Confirm privacy and data settings as shown below.

- Click on **Continue**, tick mark if you want to power up your WooCommerce store, and click on **Continue**.

- Click on the **Connect MailPoet **button.

- Now, you will be redirected to the MailPoet Account Page.

## Getting the MailPoet API Key

- Either login to your MailPoet Account or create a new account .

- Once you’re logged in, you have to add a **plan**, provide the details of the website, and **activate **it.

- You will see the below interface once you **activate **the plan.

- Copy this key to your clipboard and enter it to activate the **MailPoet account.**

- Once you have entered the activation key, now you will connected to the **MailPoet **as shown below.

- Go to **EverestForms **> **Settings **> **Integration **> **MailPoet**. You will get to the following screen after you click on **setting**s icon. You can tick mark the option and click on **Save**.

- Now, **MailPoet **will be connected to **EverestForms**.

### Connect MailPoet to your contact forms

Once you have connected the OnePageCRM to the Everest Forms settings, you need to create a form to connect it to the **OnePageCRM **. You can connect your existing forms as well. To do this, go to the following location:

All Forms > Choose a Form > Integration > MailPoet

- Click on side arrow in MailPoet, and enable **MailPoet**.

- To view the list of Subscribers, go to **WP Dashboard** > **MailPoet **> **Subscribers**.

## iContact

<https://docs.everestforms.net/docs/icontact/>

This extension allows you to directly send entry info from Everest Forms to your iContact account. iContact assists in growing your audience with personalized, automated messages, driving leads, and product sales.

## Installation

- Firstly, you need to purchase the Everest Forms Pro plugin.

- After the successful purchase, you will get the plugin zip file under your WPEverest account page.

- Now, you can download the **Everest Forms Pro** from there.

- Through your WordPress Dashboard, visit **Plugins -> Add New -> Upload** and then choose the downloaded zip file and then install and activate it.

- Now go to **Everest Forms > Add-ons > All Features.**

- Search iContact add-ons and install them.

## Setup and Configuration.

Once you have activated the iContact integration, go to Everest Forms > Settings > Integration > iContact and click on the settings button. This will take you to the configuration screen for the iContact integration.

You will get the following screen.

### Get the iContact APi Credentials

- Go to https://app.icontact.com/icp/core/registerapp . [Make sure you are logged in]

- Click on the **Create **button on the **Custom API Integration** option.

You will then automatically get all the required credentials. These are marked in the image below.

- Copy these keys to a clipboard and add it on the Everest Forms > Settings > Integration > iContact.

- Click on **Connect to iContact.**

It will then be connected to the Everest Forms. If you want to disconnect this app, you can click on the **Disconnect **button on the far right.

Similarly, you can add multiple connections.

### Connect iContact to your contact forms

Once you have connected the iContact app to the Everest Forms settings, you need to create a form to connect it to the iContact. You can connect your existing forms as well. For this, go to the following location.

All Forms > Choose a Form > Integration > iContact

- Click on **Add New Connection.**

- Provide a nickname for the connection.

- Now, you have to choose the account, list, and map the form fields as required.

- Click on **Save.**

#### How to use conditional logic for iContact connections?

To use conditional logic, enable the option by ticking the ‘**Use Conditional Logic’ **option at the bottom of every connection you make.

In the above example, the form sends data to the iContact account only if the First Name is ‘Everest’.

Note: You can add more than one connections.

## GetResponse

<https://docs.everestforms.net/docs/getresponse/>

The GetResponse Add-on for Everest Forms links your WordPress forms to your GetResponse account effortlessly. So, you can add users collected through the forms to any email list or interest group in GetResponse.

## Installation

- Firstly, you need to purchase the Everest Forms Pro plugin.
- After the successful purchase, you will get the plugin zip file under your WPEverest account page.
- Now, you can download the Everest forms pro plugin and **GetResponse** add-on.
- Through your WordPress Dashboard, visit **Plugins -> Add New -> Upload** and then choose the downloaded zip file and then install and activate it.
- Now you are ready to use this add-on for your site.

**Alternative Method:**

- Once you have entered the Everest Forms Pro license on your site, go to **Everest Forms > Add-ons**.
- Search for the ‘**GetResponse**‘ add-on.
- Click on ‘**Install**‘.
- Once the installation is finished, click on ‘**Activate**‘. The add-on will be activated.

## Setup and Configuration

Before we continue, you will need an API key for GetResponse to be connected with the Everest Forms.

### Creating a GetResponse API key

- Log in or Sign Up to your GetResponse account .
- Click on the **Tools** menu and click on ‘**Integration and APIs**‘.

- Click the **Generate API key** button.
- **Name** your key. The name is up to you. It’s a good idea to use a name that will help you keep track of all the API keys you generate.

### Integrating the GetResponse with Everest Forms

Once you have generated and copied the API Key from the GetResponse account, go to **Everest Forms > Settings > Integration > GetResponse**. Add the API Key and nickname and click on ‘**Connect to GetResponse’.**

After this, your connection has been secured. You can disconnect by clicking on the disconnect button.

### Adding Connections for individual forms

Once you have set up the required credentials on the main settings, it’s time for you to add a new connection for your forms. For this, go to the required form’s editor page. Click on ‘**Integration’ **from the available tabs. You will find an option called ‘**GetResponse**‘ from which you can add a new connection.

Click on the ‘**Add New Connection**‘ button and a pop-up will appear. Add the name of the connection

Click on ‘**OK**‘ after adding the name and the connection is added

Now, select the required account, lists and then map the fields accordingly. You can also map custom fields from the GetResponse along with the tags and autoresponder Day.

### How to use conditional logic for GetResponse connections?

To use conditional logic, enable the option by ticking the ‘**Use Conditional Logic’ **option at the bottom of every connection you make.

In the above example, the form sends data to the GetResponse account only if the First Name is ‘Everest’.

Note: You can add more than one connections.

## Sendinblue/Brevo

<https://docs.everestforms.net/docs/sendinblue/>

The Sendinblue Add-on for Everest Forms links your WordPress forms to your Sendinblue account effortlessly. So, you can add users collected through the forms to any email list or interest group in Sendinblue.

## Installation

- Firstly, you need to purchase the Everest Forms Pro plugin.

- After the successful purchase, you will get the plugin zip file under your WPEverest account page.

- Now, you can download the Everest forms pro plugin and **Sendinblue** add-on.

- Through your WordPress Dashboard, visit **Plugins -> Add New -> Upload** and then choose the downloaded zip file and then install and activate it.

- Now you are ready to use this add-on for your site.

**Alternative Method:**

- Once you have entered the Everest Forms Pro license on your site, go to **Everest Forms > Add-ons**.

- Search for the ‘**Sendinblue**‘ add-on.

- Click on ‘**Install**‘.

- Once the installation is finished, click on ‘**Activate**‘. The add-on will be activated.

## Setup and Configuration

Before we continue, you will need an API key for Sendinblue to be connected with the Everest Forms.

### Creating a Sendinblue API key

- Log in or Sign Up to your Sendinblue account.

- Click on your name at the top-right side of the screen.

- Click **SMTP & API**

- Under the **API keys** tab, click **+ CREATE A NEW API KEY**.

- Name your API key.

- Click **Generate**.

- Copy your API key and **save it** somewhere safe.

- **Note:** your API v3 key is only visible during this time.

### Integrating the Sendinblue with Everest Forms

Once you have generated and copied the API Key from the Sendinblue account, go to **Everest Forms > Settings > Integration > Sendinblue**. Add the API Key and nickname and click on ‘**Connect to Sendinblue’.**

After this, your connection has been secured. You can disconnect by clicking on the disconnect button.

### Adding Connections for individual forms

Once you have set up the required credentials on the main settings, it’s time for you to add a new connection for your forms. For this, go to the required form’s editor page. Click on ‘**Integration’ **from the available tabs. You will find an option called ‘**Sendinblue**‘ from which you can add a new connection.

Click on the ‘**Add New Connection**‘ button and a pop-up will appear. Add the name of the connection

Click on ‘**OK**‘ after adding the name and the connection is added

Now, select the required account, lists and then map the fields accordingly.

### How to use conditional logic for Sendinblue connections?

To use conditional logic, enable the option by ticking the ‘**Use Conditional Logic’ **option at the bottom of every connection you make.

In the above example, the form sends data to the Sendinblue account only if the First Name is ‘Everest’.

Note: You can add more than one connections.
Double Optin has now been enabled in the connections.

## Constant Contact

<https://docs.everestforms.net/docs/constant-contact/>

The Constant Contact Add-on for Everest Forms links your WordPress forms to your Constant Contact account effortlessly. So, you can add users collected through the forms to any email list or interest group in Constant Contact.

## Installation

- Firstly, you need to purchase the Everest Forms Pro plugin.
- After the successful purchase, you will get the plugin zip file under your WPEverest account page.
- Now, you can download the Everest forms pro plugin and **Constant Contact** add-on.
- Through your WordPress Dashboard, visit **Plugins -> Add New -> Upload** and then choose the downloaded zip file and then install and activate it.
- Now you are ready to use this add-on for your site.

**Alternative Method:**

- Once you have entered the Everest Forms Pro license on your site, go to **Everest Forms > Add-ons**.
- Search for the ‘**Constant Contact**‘ add-on.
- Click on ‘**Install**‘.
- Once the installation is finished, click on ‘**Activate**‘. The add-on will be activated.

## Setup and Configuration

Before we continue, you will need a client ID for Constant Contact to be connected with the Everest Forms.

### Getting Client ID and Secret

- Log in or Sign up for the Constant Contact .
- Go to the Developer Console of Constant Contact from here .
- Click on ‘**My Applications’.**

- Click on ‘**New Application’**.

- Fill in the Application name and click ‘**Create’. **Do not tweak with other settings here.

- You will be redirected to the ‘**My Application Dashboard**‘.
- Click on the application you have just created or, click on Edit.

- Add the Redirect URL and click on ‘**Save’.**

URL Formats:
Redirect URL: https://yoursite.com/wp-admin/?evf_constant_contact_auth=1

- Copy the Client ID and click on ‘**Generate Client Secret’. **
- Copy the generated client secret and keep it safe for the next steps.

### Integrating the Constant Contact with Everest Forms

Once you have generated and copied the Client ID and secret from the Constant Contact account, go to **Everest Forms > Settings > Integration > Constant Contact**. Add the Client ID and click on ‘**Get Access Code’.**

Now, add the access code on the ‘**Constant Contact Access Code’ **option and the client secret ID on the ‘**Constant Contact Client Secret’ **option. Add a nickname and click on ‘**Connect to Constant Contact’. **Now, the connection will be created successfully.

### Adding Connections for individual forms

Once you have set up the required credentials on the main settings, it’s time for you to add a new connection for your forms. For this, go to the required form’s editor page. Click on ‘**Integration’ **from the available tabs. You will find an option called ‘Constant Contact‘ from which you can add a new connection.

- Click on the ‘**Add New Connection**‘ button and a pop-up will appear. Add the name of the connection.

- Click on ‘**OK**‘ after adding the name and the connection is added.

Now, select the required account, lists and then map the fields accordingly. Also, you can map the Everest Forms fields with Constant Contact’s custom fields.

#### How to use conditional logic for Constant Contact connections?

To use conditional logic, enable the option by ticking the ‘**Use Conditional Logic’ **option at the bottom of every connection you make.

In the above example, the form sends data to the Constant Contact account only if the First Name is ‘Everest’.

Note: You can add more than one connections.

## Drip

<https://docs.everestforms.net/docs/drip/>

Drip is a Ecommerce CRM created for establishing scalable, profitable, and personal interactions with your consumers. Now, it can be integrated with the Everest Forms.

## Installation

- Firstly, you need to purchase the Everest Forms Pro plugin.
- After the successful purchase, you will get the plugin zip file under your WPEverest account page.
- Now, you can download the Everest forms pro plugin and **Drip **add-on from there.
- Through your WordPress Dashboard, visit **Plugins -> Add New -> Upload** and then choose the downloaded zip file and then install and activate it.
- Now you are ready to use this add-on for your site.

**Alternative Method:**

- Once you have entered the Everest Forms Pro license on your site, go to **Everest Forms > Add-ons**.
- Search for the ‘**Drip**‘ add-on.
- Click on ‘**Install**‘.
- Once the installation is finished, click on ‘**Activate**‘. The add-on will be activated.

## Setup and Configuration

You will need to have a Drip API in order to integrate the Everest Forms with the Drip. Follow the steps below for this.

### Setting up the API Key

- Sign in to the Drip account, or create one from ** here. **
- Click on **Account Name > User Settings** on the top right.

- **Copy the API key** to a clipboard.

### Integrating the Drip with Everest Forms

Once you have generated and copied the API key from the Drip account, go to **Everest Forms > Settings > Integration > Drip**. Add the API key to the ‘Drip API Key’ box. Also, add a nickname besides the API key box.

Now, click on ‘**Connect to Drip’** to integrate the Drip.

Note: You can add multiple API keys from the settings.

### Adding Connections for individual forms

Once you have set up the API key on the main settings, it’s time for you to add a new connection for your forms. For this, go to the required form’s editor page. Click on ‘**Integration’ **from the available tabs. You will find an option called ‘Drip‘ from which you can add a new connection.

- Click on the ‘**Add New Connection**‘ button and a pop-up will appear. Add the name of the connection.

- Click on ‘**OK**‘ after adding the name and the connection is added.

- **Select Account: **Select the available Drip accounts for connecting the form.
- **Select List**: Select one of the available lists.
- **List Fields**: Map the matching fields from the form fields.
- **Custom Fields: **Match the Everest Forms fields with the Drip custom fields from the available lists of the custom fields.
- **EU Consent:** You can either grant or deny the EU Consent. Or, keep it as default.

#### How to use conditional logic for Drip connections?

To use conditional logic, enable the option by ticking the ‘**Use Conditional Logic’ **option at the bottom of every connection you make.

In the above example, the form sends data to the Drip account only if the First Name is ‘Everest’.

Note: You can add more than one connections.

## Campaign Monitor

<https://docs.everestforms.net/docs/campaign-monitor/>

**Everest Forms Campaign Monitor** add-on allows you to synchronize Everest Forms with Campaign Monitor.

## Installation

- Firstly, you need to purchase the Everest Forms pro plugin.

- After the successful purchase, you will get the plugin zip file under your WPEverest account page.

- Now, you can download the Everest Forms pro plugin from there.

- Through your WordPress Dashboard, visit **Plugins -> Add New -> Upload** and then choose the downloaded zip file and then install and activate it.

- Now go to **Everest Forms > Add-ons -> All Features.**

- Search the **CampaignMonitor **module and act ivate it by clicking on the **toggle **button.

Now, follow the instructions below to **integrate Campaign Monitor with Everest Forms**:

## Set up Campaign Monitor Account:

To use this feature, you must have a Campaign Monitor Account that you will need to connect with the Everest Forms.

If you already have an Account then please find the **Client ID** and the** API key** of your **Campaign Monitor account** since you will need them for connection. You can find them in your Campaign Monitor account by following this doc: https://help.campaignmonitor.com/api-keys

If you do not have a Campaign Monitor Account then you will need to create an account first and then come back to this documentation to set up the connection.

## Configuring Campaign Monitor Account in Everest Forms

After you have got the keys, you will need to enter the **Client ID and API key** to **Everest Forms** settings.

Navigate to **Everest Forms->Settings->Integration->Campaign Monitor** and click on **Add New Connection **button.

Enter the **Client ID and API Key,** and **Campaign Monitor Nick Name** and click on **Connect to Campaign Monitor**.

You can also **connect multiple Campaign Monitor API**.

## Integrating Campaign Monitor Lists with Forms

After you have **added the keys** to the **Everest Forms settings**, now you need to** connect it to the contact form** you made.

To do so, **Click** on **Everest Forms** > **All Forms** >**(click on the form you want to connect to)**

Then, go to **Integration->Campaign Monitor** and click on **Add new connection.** Give a name to the connection.

On the right, you can **Select Account** with which you have created your list. Also, you can add a new account from there.

Now, on the **Select List** option, choose the **Campaign Monitor list** that you created.

Finally, map **Everest Forms** fields with **Campaign Monitor List Fields**.

## Conditional Logic for Adding Subscribers

**Use Conditional Logic**: You may want users to **subscribe to Campaign Monitor only if **they fill certain fields with certain values. For example, in the above case (see image above), the users will only be added to the Campaign Monitor list if they enter **Harry** in the **First Name** input.

After the setup is complete, the users can submit the form and their submission will be recorded into Campaign Monitor list.

## MailerLite

<https://docs.everestforms.net/docs/mailerlite/>

Everest Forms MailerLite add-on allows you to synchronize Everest Forms with MailerLite.

## Installation

- Firstly, you need to purchase the Everest Forms pro plugin.
- After the successful purchase, you will get the plugin zip file under your WPEverest account page.
- Now, you can download the Everest Forms pro plugin and MailerLite add-on from there.
- Through your WordPress Dashboard, visit **Plugins -> Add New -> Upload** and then choose the downloaded zip file and then install and activate it.
- Now you are ready to use this add-on for your site.

Now, follow the instructions below to **integrate MailerLite with Everest Forms**:

## Set up MailerLite Account:

To use this feature, you must have a MailerLite Account that you will need to connect with the Everest Forms.

If you already have an Account then please find the** API key** of your **MailerLite account** since you will need it for connection. You can find it in you MailerLite account by following this doc: http://help.mailerlite.com/article/show/35040-where-can-i-find-the-api-key

If you do not have a MailerLite Account then you will need to create an account first and then come back to this documentation to setup the connection.

## Configuring MailerLite Account in Everest Forms

After you have got the key, you will need to enter the ** API key** to **Everest Forms** settings.

Navigate to **Everest Forms->Settings->Integration->MailerLite** and click on **Add New Connection **button.

Enter the **API Key,** and **MailerLite Nick Name** and click on **Connect to MailerLite**.

You can also **connect multiple MailerLite API**.

## Integrating MailerLite Lists with Forms

**Note:** By default, MailerLite has a contact list where the subscribers are added. However, you can create other lists in your MailerLite Account. The created list will be shown in the MailerLite Individual Form Settings after you connect it to the Everest Forms.

After you have **added the keys** to the **Everest Forms settings**, now you need to** connect it to the contact form** you made.

To do so, **Click** on **Everest Forms** > **All Forms** >**(click on the form you want to connect)**

Then, go to **Integration->MailerLite** and click on **Add new connection.** Give a name to the connection.

On the right, you can **Select Account** with which you have created your list. Also, you can add a new account from there.

Now, on the **Select List** option, choose the **MailerLite list** that you created.

Finally, map **Everest Forms** fields to **MailerLite List Fields**.

## Conditional Logic for Adding Subscribers

**Use Conditional Logic**: You may want users to **subscribe to MailerLite only if **they fill certain fields with certain values. For example, in the above case (see image above), the users will only be added to the Active Campaign list if they enter **J**ack in the **First Name** input.

## Active Campaign

If you do not have an Active Campaign Account then you will need to create an account first and then come back to this documentation to set up the connection.

## Configuring Active Campaign Account in Everest Forms

After you have got the keys, you will need to enter the **API URL and API key** to **Everest Forms** settings.

## Integrating Active Campaign Lists with Forms

**Note:** By default, Active Campaign has a contact list where the subscribers are added. However, you can create other lists in your Active Campaign Account. The created list will be shown in the Active Campaign Individual Form Settings after you connect it to the Everest Forms.

After you have **added the keys** to the **Everest Forms settings**, now you need to** connect it to the contact form** you made.

To do so, **Click** on **Everest Forms** > **All Forms** >**(click on the form you want to connect)**

Now, on the **Select List** option, choose the **Active Campaign list** that you created.

Finally, map **Everest Forms** fields to **Active Campaign List Fields**.

You can also **add a Note** after mapping the fields. The Note will be sent to Active Campaign list whenever a subscriber is added.

## Conditional Logic for Adding Subscribers

**Use Conditional Logic**: You may want users to **subscribe to Active Campaign only if **they fill certain fields with certain values. For example, in the above case (see image above), the users will only be added to the Active Campaign list if they enter **John** in the **First Name** input.

## ConvertKit

<https://docs.everestforms.net/docs/convertkit/>

Everest Forms ConvertKit addon allows you to synchronize the Everest Forms with ConvertKit.

## Installation

- Firstly, you need to purchase the Everest Forms pro plugin.
- After the successful purchase, you will get the plugin zip file under your WPEverest account page.
- Now, you can download the Everest forms pro plugin and ConverKit addon from there.
- Through your WordPress Dashboard, visit **Plugins -> Add New -> Upload** and then choose the downloaded zip file and then install and activate it.
- Now you are ready to use this add-on for your site.

## Setup and Configuration

Once, you have completed the above mentioned task of installing and activating the plugin, now let’s move ahead on setting up this add-on for your site.

**Firstly**, you need to sign into your ConvertKit account and generate your API key. This is what will allow the plugin to securely access your ConvertKit forms. Once signed in visit the Account page and copy your API key. You can also find your API secret in your ConvertKit account by clicking “Show secret”.

Note: Wanna know how to create a form in ConvertKit?

Then, you need to enter the ConvertKit API. Navigate to** Everest Forms->Settings->Integration->ConvertKit.** Enter the ConvertKit API and ConvertKit Nick Name and connect to ConvertKit. You can connect to multiple ConvertKit APIs.

Now, let us move into mapping everest forms fields to ConvertKit list fields. Navigate to **Everest Forms->Select a form->Integration->ConvertKit.**

On the left panel, you can select account to subscribe the users. Also, you can add new account from there. Select a form in ConvertKit where you want to add the subscribers, and map the everest forms fields to your ConvertKit list fields.

**Options:Use Conditional Logic**: You may want to subscribe the users only if they fill certain fields. For example, in the figure above, the users will only be added to the ConvertKit list if they check Subscribe to our newsletter checkbox.

**How to add ‘subscribe to convertkit’ field?**

You can drag ‘checkboxes’ field and enter the subscribe to our newsletters in choices. Assign any label to it and from the advanced settings, hide label.

## MailChimp

<https://docs.everestforms.net/docs/mailchimp/>

Everest Forms MailChimp addon allows you to synchronize Everest Forms with MailChimp.

## Installation

- Firstly, you need to purchase the Everest Forms Pro plugin.

- After the successful purchase, you will get the plugin zip file under your WPEverest account page.

- Now, you can download the Everest Forms Pro plugin and MailChimp add-on from there.

- Through your WordPress Dashboard, visit **Plugins -> Add New -> Upload** and then choose the downloaded zip file, and then install and activate it.

- Now you are ready to use this add-on for your site.

Now, follow the instructions below to **integrate MailChimp with Everest Forms**:

- Setup Account in MailChimp

- Configuring MailChimp account in Everest Forms

- Integrating MailChimp Lists in Forms

- Integrating MailChimp Groups

## Setup Account in MailChimp

Once, you have completed the above-mentioned task of installing and activating the plugin, now let’s move ahead on setting up this add-on for your site.

Firstly, To properly set up your organization’s MailChimp integration you will first need your MailChimp API Key. To locate your API Key please follow the steps below:

**1**. Login to your MailChimp account via https://mailchimp.com

**2**. Once logged in to MailChimp, click on the Account Name at the top of the left-hand sidebar and select Profile.

**3**. Click on Extras and a drop-down will appear. From here, select **API** Keys. Under Your **API** Keys, you’ll find your **API** Key listed in the table below.

## Configuring MailChimp account in Everest Forms

Then, you need to enter the **MailChimp API** to **Everest Forms** settings.

Navigate to **Everest Forms->Settings->Integration->Mailchimp** and click on **Add New Connection **button.

Enter the **MailChimpAPI** and **MailChimp Nick Name** and click on **Connect to MailChimp**.

You can connect to multiple MailChimp API.

## Integrating MailChimp Lists with Forms

Now, you need to integrate your MailChimp List to your forms.

Note: Before you start this step, please make sure you create your audience lists on your **MailChimp** account. Otherwise, you won’t be able to select the **MailChimp lists** for your forms in **Everest Forms**.

If you don’t know how to create MailChimp Lists, please read MailChimp’s tutorial on Audience and Lists .

After you create a list on your **MailChimp** account, go to **Everest Forms** and select the form you want.

Then, go to **Integration->MailChimp** and click on **Add new connection.**

On the right, you can **Select Account** with which you have created your list. Also, you can add a new account from there.

Now, on the **Select List** option, choose the **MailChimp list** that you created.

Doing this will map **Everest Forms** fields to **MailChimp List Fields**. And, the subscribers to your MailChimp List.

#### **Options:**

##### **Use double opt-in**

The double opt-in process includes two steps. In **step 1**, a potential subscriber fills out your forms. In **step 2**, they’ll receive a confirmation email and click a link to verify their email, which is added to your MailChimp list.

##### **Use Conditional Logic**

You may want to subscribe to the users only if they fill certain fields. For example, in the figure above, the users will only be added to the MailChimp list if they check to Subscribe to our newsletter checkbox.

## Integrating Mailchimp Groups

Furthermore, this add-on also supports the Mailchimp **Groups** . If you want to send users to your Mailchimp groups with the form fields. Creating user groups allows you to separate and manage user types.

For this, just go to the **Integrations** tab in the form builder. If you already have created a group in Mailchimp, then it will be displayed in the **Select Groups** option in the Mailchimp tab. Here, you can easily select the Mailchimp group that you want to include.
